claim: Let \(X\sim\operatorname{Cauchy}(\mu,\sigma)\) with \(\sigma>0\). The positive-integer moment claims in Jayakumar, Samuel, and Thomas (2026), Theorem 3.1 and the dependent central-moment theorem, are not valid as ordinary expectations: for every integer \(r\ge1\), \(\mathbb E|X|^r=\infty\), so \(\mathbb E[X^r]\) is not a finite Lebesgue expectation and \(\mathbb E[X]\) is undefined. Their proof already fails at equation (3.2), because inversion of the Cauchy density is two-valued: \(x=\mu\pm\sigma\sqrt{1/(\pi\sigma f_X(x))-1}\); the displayed plus branch equals \(\mu+|x-\mu|\) and represents only \(x\ge\mu\). The sharp complex-power replacement is that, for the principal power, \(\mathbb E[X^z]=(\mu+i\sigma)^z\) holds exactly throughout the absolute-integrability strip \(-1<\operatorname{Re}z<1\). Hence the values \((\mu+i\sigma)^r\) at positive integers are analytic continuations of a legitimate fractional-moment identity, not ordinary Cauchy moments.
integrity: The integer-moment nonexistence, the two-valued density inversion, and the fractional strip identity were independently reconstructed. The fractional-moment literature was used to separate known background from the new correction. No independent external audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The correction concerns ordinary Lebesgue expectations and the cited population-moment theorems. It does not address generalized principal-value or finite-part functionals, and it does not claim novelty for the pre-existing theory of fractional complex moments.
title: A sharp correction to the LOTUS Cauchy moment theorem
